content.title: Table A5 - Revised recommendations (ESC acute coronary syndrome/MI guidance summary)

sections.Imaging for suspected NSTE-ACS: In patients with no recurrence of chest pain, normal ECG and normal levels of cardiac troponin but still suspected ACS, a non-invasive test (preferably with imaging) for inducible ischemia or CCTA is recommended before deciding on an invasive approach. In patients with suspected ACS, non-elevated or uncertain hs-cTn, no ECG changes and no recurrence of pain, incorporating CCTA or a non-invasive stress imaging test as part of the initial workup should be considered.
sections.Timing of invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS: An early invasive strategy within 24 h is recommended in patients with high-risk criteria (diagnosis of NSTEMI per diagnostic algorithm, ongoing ischemia, dynamic ST/T changes, transient ST-elevation, GRACE risk score >140).
sections.Antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy i: A potent P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor), or clopidogrel if not available/contraindicated, is recommended before (or at latest at the time of) PCI and maintained over 12 months unless contraindicated. Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in patients undergoing a primary PCI strategy.
sections.Long-term antithrombotic therapy: After stent implantation in patients undergoing DAPT, stopping aspirin after 3–6 months should be considered depending on ischemic and bleeding risks. In event-free patients after 3–6 months of DAPT who are not high ischemic risk, SAPT (preferably with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor) should be considered.
sections.Cardiac arrest and out-of-hospital cardi: Delayed rather than immediate angiography should be considered in haemodynamically stable patients without ST-elevation successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Targeted temperature management is recommended for comatose survivors (temperature control between 32–36°C for at least 24 h).
sections.In-hospital management: When echocardiography is suboptimal/inconclusive, alternative imaging (CMR preferably) should be considered.
sections.Management of multivessel disease in hae: Routine revascularization of non-IRA lesions should be considered in STEMI patients with multivessel disease before hospital discharge; complete revascularization recommended either during the index PCI or within 45 days.
sections.Acute coronary syndrome comorbid conditi: Glucose-lowering therapy should be considered in ACS patients with persistent hyperglycemia (blood glucose >10 mmol/L or >180 mg/dL). Episodes of hypoglycemia should be avoided.

abbreviations_and_notes.examples: NSTE-ACS = non-ST-elevation ACS; CCTA = coronary CT angiography; hs-cTn = high-sensitivity cardiac troponin; PCI = percutaneous coronary intervention; DAPT = dual antiplatelet therapy; SAPT = single antiplatelet therapy; IRA = infarct-related artery; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; STEMI = ST-elevation myocardial infarction; GRACE = Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events.

genes.context: Multiple recommendations refer to use of a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor (e.g., prasugrel, ticagrelor, clopidogrel) before or at time of PCI and as preferred single antiplatelet therapy after initial DAPT (mentions in STEMI antiplatelet section, pre-treatment, and long-term antithrombotic therapy).
